market_view: VIX 18.7, calm but not complacent; 10y yield 4.64% near its 52-week high and dollar firm. Oil fell 7.5-8.7% in one day on easing US-Iran tensions, and chips are in a rout led by Seoul (SK Hynix -10%).

oil_gas.catalyst: none; exit signal: 'Oil Slides, European Gas Falls as US-Iran Tensions Ease' (dars.gov.et aggregator) and 'crude oil prices fall for the first time in a week' (AP News)
oil_gas.reasoning: The supply-shock catalyst behind the XOM long is reversing: tensions ease and WTI fell 7.5% in one day, still +19% in 20 days with room to give back. The handoff rule says exit on a de-escalation headline. Close XOM.

gold_miners.reasoning: No NEM-specific headline. Gold is -10.6% over 60 days, the 10y yield sits near its 52-week high and the dollar is firm, all headwinds. A 5-day bounce in miners is not a catalyst.

chips.catalyst: none; negative headlines: 'AMD, Intel and Micron extend losses as chip stocks get clobbered' (CNBC), 'SK Hynix Shares Tumble 10%'
chips.reasoning: Sector rout with no NVDA-specific positive catalyst; NVDA -5% yesterday. Big Tech capex reports this week add variance, not direction. Do not guess a rebound.

pharma.catalyst: Continuing hold from 2026-07-23: retatrutide succeeded in two more Phase 3 obesity trials (Eli Lilly, July 23). Nothing today contradicts it; generic drug tariffs from 2028 do not hit LLY's branded franchise.
pharma.reasoning: Hold LLY to the planned window end (around 2026-08-06). Health care ETF near a 52-week high; LLY Q2 earnings in early August add variance. FDA compounding-peptide panel news is minor and unclear for LLY.

copper_uranium.catalyst: none for FCX; 'Cameco gets UBS upgrade on strengthening uranium bull case' (Yahoo Finance) concerns CCJ, not the leader
copper_uranium.reasoning: Copper is steady (+0.3% 1d, +3.2% 20d) with no supply shock or China news. The broker upgrade is for CCJ, which is not the leader. Tariffs on 60+ partners are a demand risk.

would_change_my_mind: A renewed Hormuz or Red Sea attack headline that reverses the de-escalation would justify re-entering XOM; a negative LLY safety, pricing or earnings headline would end the pharma hold.

handoff.what_changed: US-Iran tensions eased: WTI -7.5% and Brent -8.7% on July 27 (oil's first fall in a week), so the XOM long is closed on the de-escalation rule. Chips were clobbered (SK Hynix -10%, NVDA -5%). An EU-US trade deal was announced, and Trump plans generic-drug tariffs from 2028.

chips.why: Sector rout and no NVDA-specific positive catalyst.

pharma.why: Retatrutide Phase 3 wins (July 23); no contrary news; confidence 0.53.

copper_uranium.why: No FCX catalyst; the UBS upgrade is for CCJ, which is not the leader.

lessons.rule: Hypothesis only: oil longs opened on a named supply-shock escalation headline (sanctions, ship attacks) win over 10 days.
lessons.evidence: XOM 2026-07-07 net +6.82% (basket +8.64%); XOM 2026-07-10 net +12.76% (basket +10.51%). Both in the same Iran episode; below 5 cases, does not change calls.
